title: Flatness of a module over a glueing pair is detected by its two localizations
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a glueing pair (R -> R', f) and an arbitrary R-module M that is not assumed glueable, and asserts that M is flat over R exactly when M tensor_R R' is flat over R' and M_f is flat over R_f (source lines 25707-25713). One direction is base change, but the other forces the proof to first reduce to the glueable case: it introduces the glued module M-tilde, and if that is flat it applies the flat Tors criterion to the sequence 0 -> Ker(M -> M-tilde) -> M -> M-tilde -> 0 to conclude that Ker(M -> M-tilde) tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) vanishes, whence M = M-tilde by the faithfulness lemma (proof lines 25716-25727). The substantive part is then the Tors computation. From the exact sequence 0 -> R -> R' oplus R_f -> (R')_f -> 0 the proof reads off that f is a nonzerodivisor on Tor_1^R(R', N) and invertible on Tor_i^R(R', N) for i >= 2 (proof lines 25733-25744), transfers that to Tor_i^R(M tensor_R R', N) using flatness of M tensor_R R' over R' together with the change-of-rings spectral sequence and the Lazard filtered-colimit description (proof lines 25745-25755), and finally feeds it into the long exact Tors sequence of the glueable sequence 0 -> M -> M tensor_R R' oplus M_f -> M tensor_R (R')_f -> 0 to force Tor_1^R(M, N) = 0 (proof lines 25756-25770). The non-routine content is the two-step comparison of the f-action on the two families of Tor modules, which is what makes the Tors criterion applyable.
